judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three separate accrual rules keyed to Substantial Completion and the final Certificate, and the transcription is badly broken in the third limb, so the deemed accrual dates are hard to read as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.6.3 makes the arbitration deadline turn on this paragraph, and 12.2.5 distinguishes the correction period from the limitation period, so the provisions interlock but do not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 30-day trigger with four enumerated grounds, though ground .3 depends on payment 'within the time stated in the Contract Documents'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.3 leaves the payment dates blank and Addendum 12.2.2 recasts final payment timing, while Agreement 13.1 caps what the Contractor may recover on such a termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The threshold — suspensions constituting 'more than 100 percent of the total number of days scheduled for completion or 120 days in any 365-day period, whichever is less' — is oddly expressed and hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on a schedule for completion that is fixed differently in Agreement 4.3 and Addendum 4.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Persistently failed to fulfill the Owner's obligations ... with respect to matters important to the progress of the Work' is a doubly evaluative trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recovery is by cross-reference to 14.1.3, which Agreement 13.1 caps by reference to the 13.2 calculation, so the remedy is set in two places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: After three specific grounds the list closes with 'otherwise is guilty of substantial breach of a provision of the Contract Documents', a general catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is exactly the ejusdem generis problem, and 'persistently or repeatedly' is unmeasured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 6.5 gives the Owner a separate right to terminate 'in Owner's sole and absolute discretion' if the Preliminary Budget is unacceptable, a route outside this ostensibly comprehensive termination scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Finish the Work by whatever reasonable method the Owner may deem expedient' combines an objective and a subjective standard in one phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.2 caps the amount payable on a for-cause termination and A201 5.4.1 governs the subcontract assignment this paragraph invokes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole calculation turns on 'the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum', a figure the paragraph assumes to be fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In this cost-plus contract the Contract Sum is Cost of the Work plus Fee with a Guaranteed Maximum Price of 'N/A', and Agreement 13.2 prescribes a different and capped calculation for the same termination, so two incompatible measures apply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but plainly stated power to suspend 'for such period of time as the Owner may determine'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.4 supplements it by requiring GMP and Contract Time increases and by redefining 'profit' as the Contractor's Fee, though the GMP is blank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence conferring an unconditional convenience termination right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 caps the payment on such a termination and Addendum 6.5 adds a further discretionary termination right, so the Owner's exit routes are stated in three places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific, concrete duties on receipt of notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 14.4.1 and with Agreement 13.3's assignment obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed' supplies no measure, and 'costs incurred by reason of such termination' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 expressly overrides this by capping the amount at what 13.2 would yield while directing that the Fee be calculated as if the Work had been fully completed, so the two payment rules for the same event differ.
